title: Stall slot lottery: permit-current check without handing over the permit file
moment: A Taipei night market's management committee draws lots each month for vacant stall slots. Applicants currently photocopy their food business registration, health-bureau permit, and ID, and the committee clerk files the stack in a cabinet, just to confirm the permit has not expired.
verifier: Night-market management committee clerk running the monthly slot allocation
predicate: Holder has a food-hygiene registration and stall permit that is valid today (expiry date after today), proven as a fresh, non-expired status
disclosed_today: Photocopy of full permit including business address, registrant name, national ID number, permit number, scope of food categories, and often a copy of the ID card
issuer: Local health bureau (e.g. Taipei City Department of Health) via its food business registration system, signing a short-lived permit-status attestation
why_zk: The committee only needs 'valid today'; a signed attestation with a short validity window lets the applicant prove freshness without the ID number, home address, or other business registrations. Weakness: the committee may be legally expected to keep a permit copy for audit, in which case selective disclosure only reduces what is shown, not what is retained; and the issuing bureau would have to build a status-attestation service.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the Australian secret ballot, eligibility is checked separately from the ballot so identity is not attached to the vote at counting; here, the permit-validity check at the gate is separated from the lottery entry so the drawn slot is not linked to the full permit file.

In HIPAA minimum-necessary, the holder of records must limit release to what a stated purpose needs but has no proof that it did; here, the stall applicant's proof plays that role by cryptographically limiting the release to 'permit current' for the slot-allocation purpose.

title: Daily gate check by the market inspector without a roster of permit holders
moment: Each evening a committee patrol officer walks the stall rows at a night market and checks that every vendor setting up has a current permit, today by reading the laminated permit card and noting names and permit numbers in a notebook that gets typed into a shared spreadsheet.
verifier: Committee patrol officer doing evening setup inspection
predicate: Vendor's food-hygiene and stall permit is current as of today, shown as a fresh presentation tied to this evening and this market
disclosed_today: Name, permit number, photo, registered address and food categories read off the card and copied into a spreadsheet kept by the committee
issuer: Local health bureau, issuing the permit credential to the vendor's phone wallet with an expiry and revocation status
why_zk: The officer needs a yes/no for tonight, not a durable log of who sells what and where they live. A presentation bound to the date and market lets the check pass without creating a spreadsheet that can be leaked or used to track vendors across markets. Weakness: the committee may have a regulatory or lease-management reason to record which permit holder occupies which stall, and many older vendors do not use smartphone wallets.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the ALA library-records policy, the library avoids keeping a readable log of who borrowed what; here, the patrol officer's nightly check plays that role by recording only a pass/fail tick rather than a roster of identified vendors.

In SameSite cookies, a credential is sent only to the issuing context so unrelated observers cannot match the holder across sites; here, the permit presentation is scoped to this one market and date so that two different markets cannot link the same vendor.

title: Platform and landlord check before a vendor joins a pop-up night market event
moment: A pop-up night market at a school grounds or temple plaza is organised by a district office contractor. Vendors from other districts apply online and upload scans of their permit and ID card; the organiser has to confirm permits are current but stores everything in a shared cloud folder.
verifier: Event organiser contractor for a temporary pop-up night market
predicate: Applicant holds a food-hygiene and stall permit that is not expired on the event date, and the freshness is shown by a recent issuer signature rather than an old scan
disclosed_today: Uploaded scan of permit and ID card, home address, mobile number, sometimes business tax registration, stored in a shared cloud folder with loose access
issuer: Health bureau of the vendor's home municipality, with the Ministry of Health and Welfare food registration platform as the signing authority
why_zk: The organiser is a short-lived contractor with weak data handling; a proof of 'current permit' removes the need for them to hold ID scans after the event. A fresh signed status also stops stale-scan fraud, where an expired permit is photographed and reused. Weakness: the PDPA and event contracts may still require the organiser to retain application records, and cross-municipality issuer coverage is not guaranteed, so some vendors would still need paper fallback.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: In the household-register proxy rule, the office may collect a copy of the principal's ID document at its own discretion; here, the event organiser plays that role by collecting ID scans simply because nothing stops it, which the permit proof would make unnecessary.

In HIPAA minimum-necessary, a holder is told to release only what a purpose needs but is left to judge what that is; here, the vendor's wallet plays that role by releasing only the 'permit current on event date' claim for the stated purpose of event admission.
